Vietnamese dinner (and thanks again!)
Aug 2026 • Couples
Quán Ăn Ngon is a very unique place, built as a sort of reconstruction of a traditional Vietnamese courtyard, with different spaces and a lively and characteristic atmosphere.

The real highlight, however, was the service. We ordered Chả Cá Hà Nội and some spring rolls to prepare with rice paper and, without the help and especially the patience of our waitress, we probably would never have understood how to eat them correctly! She showed us step by step how to assemble the spring rolls and even helped us cook the fish at the table. A truly attentive service that made the dinner even more pleasant.

We ate very well and spent about €15 per person, so the value for money is also definitely excellent.

The restaurant is very large, but it is also extremely popular, so I still recommend booking and not taking it for granted that you will find a seat. They accept credit cards.

One last practical tip: if you don't want to die of heat, or risk finding yourself in a downpour, ask for a table in the air-conditioned indoor areas.

A great experience to get closer to Vietnamese cuisine, especially thanks to a staff that doesn't just serve the dishes, but also helps you understand how to enjoy them to the fullest.

It's a pity that getting to a table was so chaotic.
Jan 2026 • Couples
This was recommended by our guide who told us she had booked a table for us. Admittedly we arrived early for our allotted time but it was clear that there was no booking. The restaurant was huge and seriously busy with locals and tourists. We took this as a good sign and agreed with one of the reception people that we sit and wait. It was chaotic. It seemed like people who had no booking were going straight to tables. Others, mainly tourists, who had booked stood around like us looking mystified.
Eventually we were shown to a table and the food was superb without being showy. We enjoyed our chat with some French guys at the next table who lived in Hanoi. Service, considering how busy they were was fine.

Insider tip:
Don't bother booking and, if you have to wait, make sure they don't forget you!

A different place to eat
Oct 2025 • Friends
We were recommended by the people of the hotel where we were staying (Mercure Hanoi La Gare Hotel) which was a few blocks away.
It has tables outside and inside the house (one floor). It impresses by its size and the number of people who work. All very well organized and everyone fulfills their task perfectly.
The menu is very varied Vietnamese food, therefore there are alternatives for all tastes. It is striking that they put ice on the beer glasses.
Prices are fine and you eat relatively quickly. You can make your first experience with chopsticks, but cutlery is also available. They accept cards.
Outside you can appreciate the different forms of cuisine there are. 
A recommended place. You're not gonna regret it.

Beware of taxis waiting for customers in front of Quan An Ngon.
Oct 2025 • Couples
On a Saturday in the beginning of October, I went to this restaurant to eat my first Vietnamese food on my first trip to Vietnam. The dishes were varied and each tasted satisfying. The time to come out was fast and the parlor staff was able to respond quickly to customer orders.
There are some things you need to be aware of at this store. I asked him to call a taxi on the way home, but he told me he needed a taxi in front of the shop and I got in the taxi, and he was a very vicious driver. The hotel is less than 15 or 20 minutes' walk away, about 1.2 kilometers. I was charged 420,000 VND for that distance, and after I thought it was too expensive, I put out a 500,000 VND bill, but they said I didn't have enough money, and when I saw the returned bill, it was 200,000 VND, and I thought I had grabbed the wrong bill from my wallet, so I put out the 500,000 VND again. They offered me 100,000 dong in change and told me that this was fine, but I don't feel comfortable. When I went back to the hotel and did the math, it was like I had taken out a 500,000 VND bill and swapped it for a 200,000 VND bill. I think the reason I gave back so much change was to make it harder to complain. I also checked the price of taxis in Hanoi on the internet, and if it is about 1 kilometer, it is about 20,000 to 30,000 VND.
It was bad that I couldn't use my glove myself, but I wanted to be introduced to the taxis I could trust customers to use. (Maybe it was on my phone or the app, but I couldn't find a hotel to go to, so it took a long time, so I asked the hotel for a taxi.) It was the first day of my trip to Hanoi, and while I was satisfied that Hanoi was a vibrant and fun city, I was filled with a lot of regret and instantly hated it.)

Hotel staff recommended
Jan 2025 • Couples
My husband and I don't stay in hotels in Hanoi, Taiping, or downtown because the road is crowded when we go to the factory. Stay in a hotel in a location that is easy to get to. It's inconvenient to go around town. Since I came all the way, I wanted to eat delicious Vietnamese food at least once, so I asked the hotel staff to make a reservation and they told me which restaurant to recommend. I was disappointed and recommended this place. If you make a reservation and go by taxi, there are many people who seem to be very popular. It spins fast, and one customer after another! But
Privately, maybe I was sorry about the food? The whole thing is sweet and persistent. Why is it so popular? - I don't know. It's strange, the biggest disappointment is the crab! The price was so high but the seasoning was so strong that the delicious crab taste was gone. Four might have been the best.
